resumen: Hanging from a bar, the knees come up towards the chest. The abs work by curling the pelvis, not just by lifting the legs.
ejecucion: Hang from the bar with hands shoulder-width apart and your body still.
Bring your knees up towards your chest, curling your pelvis up at the end.
Lower slowly, without letting your body swing.
If you start swinging, stop and begin again: momentum is doing the work.
Once you own it, you can raise straight legs instead of knees.
matices: In the cited analysis of abdominal exercises, hanging raises produced some of the highest activation of both rectus abdominis and external oblique, above traditional curl-ups. The part that counts most is the end, when the pelvis curls: raising the knees without that mostly trains the hip flexor.
